text:
Brayden Point is back off injured reserve after a short stint, activated on Nov. 17 as Conor Geekie went the other way, per Daily Faceoff. He went on IR after playing less than six minutes in Winnipeg on Nov. 8, and Tampa used the gap to give prospect Sam O'Reilly a look.

Before that, Point was quietly excellent. He has 16 points in 17 games, and Tampa takes almost 60% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances). His 3.02 points per 60 minutes sits at the top of our range for him, and his own chance quality is up from last season. Five goals on 6.6 expected is, if anything, a little light.

Evolving-Hockey offers one caution from last season: his results ran ahead of his chances, 2.4 wins against 0.7 expected, with strong teammates helping. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why Tampa likes him with the puck anyway: 67% of his entries carried in and 62% of his exits leaving with possession. He's in the 97th percentile for top skating speed. Watch his minutes in his first games back.
headline: Point is back, and his game never left
